land.text: Perak, under a British Resident from the Pangkor Treaty of 20 January 1874; Cliopatria's British Colonial Empire 1877 shape contains all 73 cells of the last Perak shape

successors.note: Perak remains a Malay sultanate under British protection and joins the Federated Malay States in 1895 (History of Perak); Cliopatria ends the row in 1876.

capitals.name: Kuala Kangsar

Kuala Kangsar is not in the gazetteer; the coordinate is approximate.

correction.text: the Perak River valley, the province of Perak

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1528: 'By 1528, a Muslim sultanate began to emerge in Perak' and Muzaffar Shah 'ascended to the throne as Muzaffar Shah I, first Sultan of Perak' (History of Perak); Cliopatria starts a year later. The same 72-cell Perak province shape. No page opened gives an area (the infobox of the Sultan of Perak page is only a ruler list), so Cliopatria's 23,820 km2 cannot be compared.

Perak province (94 percent of it) plus six border cells of Kelantan and Pahang (23,820 km2), the 'banks of the Perak River' where 'the Perak Sultanate was formed in the early 16th century'. Applies 1529-1571; the Perak sultanate's frontiers with Kedah, Selangor and Pahang are not described on any page opened.

Cell-for-cell the 1529 shape but for one swapped cell (23,792 km2). Under Acehnese pressure ('Throughout the 1570s, the Sultanate of Aceh subjected most parts of the Malay Peninsula to continual harassment'), no land change is recorded. Applies 1572-1587.

One swapped cell again (23,763 km2); 'Although Perak did fall under the authority of the Acehnese Sultanate' from 1612, Aceh's Cliopatria shape does not include Perak, so the Perak shape is right as the land of the sultan. Applies 1588-1608.

Same Perak shape for 1609-1818 (23,820 km2). Aceh invaded in 1620 and 'captured its sultan'; the VOC tin treaty of 15 December 1653 and the fort on Pangkor Island (1670) change no border; the vassalage to Aceh belongs in the Aceh dossier.

correction.text: Perak without its inland districts of Hulu Perak, held by Reman

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1819-1825: after Kedah's attack on Perak on Siam's behalf in 1818 Siam then expanded into inland Hulu Perak, and the Siamese tributary Reman, backed by Siam, controlled several inland districts after a civil war (History of Perak); a map caption has 'Perak's interior shown under Siamese tributary the Reman Kingdom, before recovery with British help in 1909'. The page gives neither a boundary nor a year for the loss; the circle round Gerik is a rough reading.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1822 shape without Hulu Perak (Reman) and the Dindings and Pangkor (British)

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria adds one Kedah border cell (23,993 km2); I remove Reman's inland districts from 1819 (see 1819) and, from 1826, the Dindings and Pangkor, ceded to the British ('The Sultan of Perak then ceded to the British Dindings and Pangkor' after Ligor's 1826 attack; the Pangkor Treaty page: 'Pulo Dinding and the islands of Pangkor were ceded to Great Britain'). Applies 1826-1872.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1873 shape without Hulu Perak and the Dindings

keyframe_review.note: Cell-for-cell the 1822 shape; the same corrections apply. The Pangkor Treaty of 20 January 1874 puts a British Resident beside the sultan but moves no further border (Larut, renamed Taiping, stays in Perak under an assistant Resident). Applies 1873-1876.

region.text: the Perak River valley: Muzaffar Shah, 'invited to rule Perak', first sultan

ledger.note: 1528: a Malacca prince founds the Sultanate of Perak. 'By 1528, a Muslim sultanate began to emerge in Perak, out of the remnants of the Malaccan Sultanate'; the Sultan of Perak page: Mahmud Shah died at Kampar in 1528 and Muzaffar Shah 'was invited to rule Perak, of which he became the first sultan'. No month or founding capital is given.

1818: Siam has Kedah attack Perak. 'In the same year as when Perak refused to send a bunga mas tribute to the Siamese court, the king Rama II of Siam had Kedah attack Perak'; Sultan Abdu'l-Malik was 'forced to surrender to a large army sent by the Sultan of Kedah, on behalf of the Siamese King' and 'Removed from exercising executive powers ... after 18 November 1818' (Sultan of Perak page).

region.text: inland Hulu Perak, which Reman, a Siamese tributary backed by Siam, controlled after a civil war

ledger.note: 1819: the inland districts of Hulu Perak pass to Reman, a Siamese tributary. Page silent on the year (after November 1818) and on the boundary; the map caption has the interior under Reman 'before recovery with British help in 1909' (outside this dossier).

region.text: the Dindings and Pangkor, now Manjung District

ledger.note: 1826: Perak cedes the Dindings and Pangkor to the British. After Ligor's 1826 attack, stopped by a small British force, 'The Sultan of Perak then ceded to the British Dindings and Pangkor'; the Burney Treaty of 1826 had 'the Siamese agreed not to attack Perak or Selangor'. The Pangkor Treaty page has 'Pulo Dinding and the islands of Pangkor were ceded to Great Britain' and a redrawn boundary in 1874 (year of the cession itself not given on the History page).

1826: Siam's pressure on Perak ends with the Burney Treaty. The attempt by Ligor, a Siamese tributary, to conquer Perak in 1826 was stopped, and Siam promised not to attack Perak or Selangor; Reman keeps the inland districts. Page silent on any recovery before 1909.

region.text: Pulo Dinding and the islands of Pangkor, boundaries redrawn

ledger.note: 1874: the Pangkor Treaty puts a British Resident in Perak and redraws the Dindings. Signed 'on 20 January 1874' aboard the Colonial Steamer Pluto; Abdullah is recognised as sultan, Raja Ismail keeps the title Sultan Muda; 'Pulo Dinding and the islands of Pangkor were ceded to Great Britain'; Larut is renamed Taiping. 'Clarke arrived in November 1873 and he put Perak, Selangor and Sungei Ujong under British protection within a year.' Protectorate status is for the British dossier's vassal event.

1876: the Perak War ends and the sultanate's independence with it. 'By mid-1876, the war ended with the capture of prominent leaders and warriors'; Sultan Abdullah and Ngah Ibrahim 'were exiled to the Seychelles'; 'Thus ended any direct opposition over British control of Perak'. The Perak sultanate continues under British protection and joins the Federated Malay States in 1895 (History of Perak); Cliopatria ends the row in 1876.

wars.name: Acehnese conquest of Perak

zones.text: Perak, which 'did fall under the authority of the Acehnese Sultanate' from 1612

wars.outcome: 'In 1620, the Acehnese sultanate invaded Perak and captured its sultan'; after Sultan Sallehuddin died in 1635 'Perak chieftains were left with no alternative but to turn to Aceh's sultan Iskandar Thani', who sent Raja Sulong as Muzaffar Shah II. Aceh's influence waned as the VOC arrived (Aceh's sultana ordered Perak to sign with the VOC in 1650; treaty of 15 December 1653).
wars.note: No border moved and Aceh's Cliopatria shape never includes Perak: a vassalage for the Aceh dossier (vassal_start 1612 or 1620 with counterpart sultanate-of-perak). The page gives no end date for Aceh's authority; 1653, the year of the VOC treaty, is the last date the page connects with the waning of Aceh's influence.

wars.name: Kedah's attack on Perak for Siam
wars.outcome: Perak's sultan was set aside after 18 November 1818; Reman, a Siamese tributary, took the inland districts. In 1821 Siam conquered Kedah; in 1826 Ligor's attack on Perak was stopped by a small British force and the Burney Treaty had Siam promise not to attack Perak or Selangor.
wars.note: Perak 'remained entirely independent of Siamese control for over two hundred years from 1612' says the page, yet its interior is shown under Reman: a disagreement inside one page.

wars.name: Larut Wars
belligerents: rival Perak chiefs and Chinese secret societies of Larut
wars.outcome: Ended by the Pangkor Treaty of 20 January 1874, which recognised Abdullah as sultan and brought a British Resident.
wars.note: 'escalated into the Larut Wars in 1861' (History of Perak). Internal war; no border moved.

wars.name: Perak War

zones.text: Pasir Salak, Bandar Bahru, Kota Lama Kanan

wars.outcome: After Birch's murder in 1875 the British took Pasir Salak on 12 December 1875 and by mid-1876 ended the resistance; Abdullah and Ngah Ibrahim were exiled to the Seychelles and Perak stayed under a British Resident.
wars.note: The infobox gives 1875-1877. British attack at Pasir Salak 7 November 1875; ambush at Kota Lama Kanan, Sayong, 4 January 1876.

certainty.note: No survey line: the Perak River basin and its tin districts, with the Hulu Perak frontier moving with Reman (from 1819) and Aceh's influence.
The Pangkor Treaty fixes the sultan's status, not a surveyed boundary; the Dindings are the only treaty-defined land.

notes:
Five pages opened (budget 5). The page titled 'Sultan of Perak' (Cliopatria's Wikipedia field) is only a ruler list; 'Perak Sultanate' redirects to it, so the state's story comes from the history of Perak (a section of the article on Perak). None of the pages gives an area, so the Cliopatria areas (about 23,800 km2) were not compared.
CLIOPATRIA: the Perak row is a flat province shape for 348 years (one swapped cell in 1572, 1588, 1609; one Kedah cell added in 1822). Not represented: Aceh's authority 1612-c.1650; Reman's hold on Hulu Perak from about 1819 (recovered 1909); the Dindings and Pangkor ceded to Britain. The shape includes six cells of Kelantan and Pahang that the pages do not support.
PAGE SILENT: capitals before the present Kuala Kangsar; the rulers 1577-1635; the end of Aceh's authority; the date and boundary of Reman's gain; whether the Dindings passed in 1826 or 1874 (the History page puts 'then ceded' after the 1826 events; the Pangkor Treaty page has the cession in the 1874 treaty); the 1876/1877 deposition date (Sultan of Perak page: 30 March 1877).
NEEDS DOSSIERS: Reman (Siamese tributary kingdom, Hulu Perak 1819-1909); the British dossier should carry vassal_start for Perak (Pangkor Treaty, 1874) and an occupation for the Perak War; the Aceh dossier should carry Perak as a vassal 1612 to c.1650.
Gazetteer: Kuala Kangsar, Gerik, Hulu Perak, the Dindings, Pangkor and Larut are not in the gazetteer (Taiping is).
